environment.description: Same Ktor service deployed inside a minimal OCI container image (distroless gcr.io/distroless/java17-debian12) with a read-only root filesystem. The container runs under a custom seccomp profile (report-svc-seccomp.json) that denies open_by_handle_at, ptrace, and restricts openat to paths matching /app/static/** and /tmp/**. The container's PID namespace is isolated and /proc is mounted with hidepid=2. The pod runs with a Kubernetes SecurityContext specifying runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, and drops ALL capabilities. The container's filesystem is assembled via a multi-stage build that copies ONLY the application JAR and a minimal /app/templates directory containing only .html files. No /etc/passwd, no /etc/shadow, no shell binaries, no environment variable secrets (secrets are injected via a CSI volume driver that mounts them at /mnt/secrets but the seccomp profile blocks openat for /mnt/secrets from the JVM process GID). The chroot-equivalent confinement means even successful SSTI expression evaluation that attempts file reads or command execution will find: no files of value, no command binaries to execute, and blocked syscalls for any escape attempt.

config.seccomp_profile: report-svc-seccomp.json (allowlist: read, write, openat[/app/static/**, /tmp/**], close, fstat, mmap, mprotect, brk, futex, epoll_*, socket, bind, listen, accept, connect[egress blocked by NetworkPolicy])
config.filesystem: read-only rootfs, /tmp as emptyDir with 10Mi limit
config.kubernetes_network_policy: egress denied to all except kube-dns:53/UDP
config.env_vars: none - secrets via CSI volume at /mnt/secrets (GID-restricted)
config.available_binaries: only JVM runtime, no sh, no bash, no cat, no curl
